# The Sacrificed — Those Who Gave Their Lives

> Every war has a person who stopped the onslaught of a great monster or demon with their own life. They are invented
> people — ox-drivers, helmsmen, shepherds, gong-players — not kings and not gods. Like Ambri's sacrifice
> (`02-chronology.md`), their names are spoken quietly at the front. Their place is played as one scenario of each campaign (`../campaigns/`).

## Bacho the Khevsur — 1871

*Iberia · "The Ninth Day" · campaign: [Thunder Mountains](../campaigns/iberia.md)*

In the autumn of 1871, in Qursha's Ravine, one head of the Father of Devis came down into the ravine — behind Amirani's back. The Khevsur Bacho stood in the throat of the ravine for nine days with thirty men, with sword and chain shirt, while Amirani fought up ahead. On the tenth day the head broke into the ravine; Bacho bound the keep's last lightning coil to his shield and walked into the devi's jaws. The head fell into the valley and never grew back. Every autumn the Khevsurs carry Bacho's shield back to the throat of the ravine.

## Engineer Adela — 1871

*Brotherhood of Listeners · "Her Own Lock" · campaign: [Forty Locks](../campaigns/listeners.md)*

On the Night of Opening Adela, an engineer of the brotherhood, opened her own lock in the valley seal — as she had been ordered. Then she saw what came up: a head of the Father of Devis, which chose neither nations nor brotherhood. Below the valley was the town where her sister lived. Adela went down into the seal and closed the lock by hand — from the inside, while the head was rising. The valley gate shut. The brotherhood struck her name from its lists. The coalition never learned of it. In the town her sister still believes Adela was a ship's engineer who died at sea.

## Naledi the Pump-Keeper — 1871

*Southern African Mountains · "The Cooled Walls" · campaign: [The Swallowed Fortress](../campaigns/southern_african.md)*

On the night in 1871 when the Kammapa swallowed the fortress, the fire of the monster's belly began to melt the walls. The pump-keeper Naledi worked the fortress's steam pumps by hand, led the people down into the deep cellars — and stayed at the pumps to cool the walls while the coal lasted. The fortress survived, and four hundred people in it. Naledi did not. The signaller Sipho, who has sent signals out of the belly ever since that night, flashes his lantern three times on that night every year — for Naledi.

## Beka the Ox-Driver — 1872

*Colchis · "The Last Yoke" · campaign: [Ambri's Furrow](../campaigns/colchis.md)*

On the Day of Ambri's Burial, as the giant was being lowered into the gate, the Father of Devis thrust his heads up from below and broke the yoke of the steam oxen. The twelfth ox, out of control, turned away from the crater's edge. The ox-driver Beka climbed onto the ox's neck, opened the steam valve by hand and turned the ox back toward Ambri — ox and Beka went down into the Wound together as Ambri's last burden. The door was sealed. Colchian ox-drivers still count twelve oxen, and quietly name a thirteenth — Beka.

## Marfa the Bell-Ringer — 1875

*Northern Slavic Lands · "The Zmei's Bridge" · campaign: [Morana's Winter](../campaigns/polianitsy.md)*

In 1875 Zmei Gorynych came down on the bridge that joined two villages, while women, children and the sledges of the sleeping men were on the bridge. The bell-ringer Marfa wound the bridge bell's rope around her hand and rang with all her strength — the zmei turned toward the sound and fell on her, in the middle of the bridge, when the column had already crossed. The bell fell into the river with the bridge. On winter nights the fishermen say the bell still rings beneath the ice.

## Samuel the Tunnel Lamp-Man — 1876

*North American Forests · "The Tunnel Collapse" · campaign: [Man and Drill](../campaigns/north_american.md)*

In 1876 a tunnel collapsed, and a snallygaster — a winged monster — came down at the tunnel mouth, where twenty workers were trapped. The lamp-man Samuel hung his lantern opposite the mouth, drew the monster off toward the forest with the light, and carried it before its eyes all night while the gang dug through the rubble. In the morning the tunnel was opened. Samuel's lantern was taken down from a tree — still burning.

## Kamila the Well-Warden — 1878

*Oghuz Lands · "The Well Lid" · campaign: [Descent into the Underworld](../campaigns/oghuz.md)*

In 1878 a spawn of Tepegöz — a one-eyed giant — came up out of a well and set off toward a camp full of people. The well-warden Kamila rode across the giant's path, loosed an arrow at its single eye and, when the giant fell to its knees, chained the well's iron lid to its leg. Both fell into the well. The lid closed over them. The Hunters of Basat keep one place in their quivers for Kamila's arrow — empty.

## Eirik the Horn-Keeper — 1879

*Northern Union · "Heimdall's Tower" · campaign: [Wolf Winter](../campaigns/northern.md)*

In the winter of 1879 Fenrir's pack took the fjord fortress at midnight, and the tower horn fell silent — the villages would no longer hear that the wolves were coming. Eirik, the old horn-keeper, climbed the tower, locked the door from inside and blew until dawn while the wolves tore down the lower floors. The nine villages of the valley were evacuated by morning. In the tower they found Eirik's horn, still warm.

## Otto the Shaft Bell-Keeper — 1879

*Prussia · "The Closed Shaft" · campaign: [Cobalt](../campaigns/prussia.md)*

In 1879 the spawn of the lindwurm came up from a deep tunnel while two hundred miners were still below. The shaft bell-keeper Otto rang the bell until the last cage came up. Then he went down himself and brought down the old kobold ore-heap in the tunnel — the stone his grandfathers used to leave in the shaft. The spawn could not cross the stone. The tunnel was sealed. To this day the shaft bell rings once too often every shift — for Otto.

## Ravi the Lantern-Keeper — 1880

*Indian Peninsula · "The Lantern Line" · campaign: [The Twenty-Fifth Night](../campaigns/indian.md)*

One night in 1880 the wind blew out the line of lanterns that held the bhuta back from the village — eight lanterns of nine. The lantern-keeper Ravi took the last burning lantern and walked the line on foot, from one to the next, through the middle of the bhuta, and lit them all again. At the ninth lantern the cold brought him down. The line burned until morning. The Night Watch still lights its lanterns starting from the right — in Ravi's direction.

## Tiit the Amber-Gatherer — 1880

*Baltic Forests and Shore · "The Black Amber Shore" · campaign: [The Released Hand](../campaigns/baltic.md)*

In 1880 the servants of the lord of the underworld came up out of the sea while amber-gatherers were on the shore — women and children, on a cold night. Tiit, an old gatherer, lit an old amber bonfire at the far end of the shore, and the resin smoke of the fire drew the servants toward him — the dark creatures followed the smoke. While he kept the fire going, the gatherers reached the village. In the morning the bonfire was still burning.

## Gilles the Bridge-Warden — 1881

*Gaul · "The Stone Bridge" · campaign: [The River Monster](../campaigns/gaul.md)*

In 1881 the Tarasque reached the town's last bridge while a column of refugees stood on it. The bridge-warden Gilles set off the explosives laid in the bridge's central arch when the monster was already on the arch — and did not run himself, because the fuse had to be held by hand. The bridge fell with the Tarasque. The refugees were already on the bank. The new bridge built in the same place is called Gilles' Bridge.

## Mixtli the Runner — 1882

*Peoples of the Mexican Valley · "The Eclipse Torch" · campaign: [The New Fire](../campaigns/mexica.md)*

During the eclipse of 1882 one section of the ring of torches went out, and the tzitzimime came down through the gap — toward the children's house. The runner Mixtli took two torches and stood in the gap, arms spread, a living post of torches, while the other runners brought new fire. The tzitzimime fell on him — and could not get through. When the ring closed, the torches were still burning in his hands.

## Aram the Stonemason — 1883

*Armenian Highlands · "The Drained Lake" · campaign: [The Lakes of the Vishaps](../campaigns/armenian.md)*

In the summer of 1883 a cloud vishap came down on a lake, and the lake was draining in a single night. The stonemason Aram knew that an old vishap stone lay fallen at the bottom of the lake — and that to raise it one man had to stay at the bottom, at the lever. He went down. The stone stood, the vishap rose into the sky with the water and vanished, and the lake came back — over Aram. The stone now bears the print of his hand, carved into the stone itself.

## Franek the Cobbler — 1883

*Lechia · "The Salt Sheep" · campaign: [The Smok's Thirst](../campaigns/lechia.md)*

In 1883 the spawn of the Smok were coming toward a riverside town, and sulphur bombs only made them stronger. The cobbler Franek remembered his grandmother's version from childhood: the dragon was not killed by sulphur, but by thirst. He stuffed sheepskins with salt, piled them on a cart and drove them himself toward the spawn's nest. The spawn ate the salt and went to the river — far from the town. Franek and his cart never came back from the nest. The town's cobblers still put one grain of salt in every new shoe.

## Iñaki the Shepherd — 1884

*Pyrenean Mountains · "The One-Eye's Flock" · campaign: [The Returned Gold](../campaigns/pyrenean.md)*

In 1884 a one-eyed giant came down on a mountain village, and the shepherd Iñaki was on the mountain path with his flock. In the fairy tale the shepherd hides from the giant under the flock. Iñaki did not hide: he ran with the sheep not toward the village but toward the mountain, with bells and shouts, and the giant chased him. The village was saved. Iñaki's bells were found at the top of the path. The next morning the flock came down to the village on its own.

## Kenta the Bridge-Warden — 1885

*Japanese Isles · "The Hundred-Leg Bridge" · campaign: [The Oni's Treasure](../campaigns/japan_isles.md)*

In 1885 the Ōmukade came over the town bridge, and under the bridge, in boats, were hundreds of refugees. The bridge-warden Kenta packed smith's charges into the bridge piers and lit the fuse himself, on the bridge, at the monster's feet — the fuse was far too short to run. The bridge fell, and the river carried the Ōmukade out to sea. The boats were saved. Every year Hidesato's Archers shoot one arrow into the water where the bridge stood.

## Bauyrzhan the Scout — 1885

*Central Asian Mountains and Steppes · "The Blind Column" · campaign: [The White Div's Dust](../campaigns/central_asian.md)*

In 1885 a whole column went into a storm wearing goggles, and divs walked through the middle of it, unseen. The scout Bauyrzhan, whose goggles had fallen off, saw them — and he was the only one who could see. He took the head of the column, turned his horse and, shouting, with his voice alone, showed everyone the way until the column was out of the valley. He himself stayed in the valley, among the divs. His voice, they say, can still be heard in the storm.

## Niko the Smith's Apprentice — 1886

*Hellenic League · "The Storm Wall" · campaign: [Typhon's Storm](../campaigns/hellenic.md)*

In the storm of 1886 Talos fell on the shore — steam was pouring from the valve in his heel, and Typhon's serpent legs were already coiling around the harbour. The smith's apprentice Niko crawled to the fallen giant's heel, shut the valve with his own hand and stayed in the jet of steam until Talos stood up and met Typhon in the sea. The steam took Niko. In the forge of Hephaestus every repair of Talos begins in his name.

## Kwame the Boatman — 1886

*West African Lands · "The Mirror Boat" · campaign: [The Written and the Spoken](../campaigns/west_african.md)*

In 1886 Ninki Nanka came up out of the river toward the trading harbour while the harbour's people were still at the market. The boatman Kwame covered his boat with a great copper mirror, sailed in front of the monster and sent its reflection down with the river current — downstream, away from the town. Ninki Nanka followed the reflection until it reached the falls. Kwame went over the falls. The Mirror Marksmen engrave his name on their mirrors.

## Hasan the Drummer — 1886

*The Ottomans · "A Drum Until Dawn" · campaign: [The Thirteen Lost Nights](../campaigns/ottoman.md)*

On a zemheri night in 1886 the karakoncolos called through the quarter with voices — the voices of mothers, brothers, the dead — and children stood at the windows. Hasan, a drummer of the mehter, went out into the street and beat his drum all night, so loud that no one in the quarter could hear a single voice. He stood among the karakoncolos himself and answered no voice. At dawn the drum lay in the street. The drummer did not. Since then, on the last night of the zemheri, the drum is beaten until dawn in every quarter.

## Tulu the Dog-Driver — 1887

*Arctic Ice and Tundra · "Thin Ice" · campaign: [Open Water](../campaigns/arctic.md)*

In 1887 a legion came up out of the open water near a village, and the villagers were running across the ice toward the shore. The dog-driver Tulu knew where the ice was thin — and drove his dog-sledge straight in front of the legion, onto the thin ice, while the people crossed on the thick. The legion chased him. The ice broke. Tulu's dogs reached the shore — the sledge was empty.

## Nora the Interpreter — 1888

*The Ring Battalion · "Eleven Tongues" · campaign: [Forty Tongues](../campaigns/ring.md)*

One night in 1888 a head of the Father of Devis broke through the battalion's southern trench. The order to fall back was given — in one language. Squads from eleven nations stood on the line, and they did not understand the order. The interpreter Nora ran along the trench — past the head — shouting the order in every language, from squad to squad. Eleven squads fell back. Nora stayed with the eleventh, where the head came down. Every new interpreter in the battalion is taught her oath: "Everyone must understand the order."

## Aarne the Furnace-Keeper — 1888

*Finnish Forests · "The Cold Furnace" · campaign: [The Stolen Sun](../campaigns/finnish.md)*

In midwinter 1888 Louhi's ice host reached the boiler of the steam sun — if the furnace went cold, the forests would freeze in a week. The furnace-keeper Aarne shovelled coal by hand all night while the ice warriors smashed the walls of the forge, and when the coal ran out he fed the fire his wooden leg and the door of his hut. In the morning the sun was lit. Aarne was found by the furnace, frozen, in the light of the embers.

## Jan the Bargeman — 1888

*The Batavi · "The Sunken Barge" · campaign: [The Water-Wolf](../campaigns/batavi.md)*

On an autumn night in 1888 the ghost-ships broke through the dike, and the water poured toward the polder where three villages slept. The bargeman Jan steered his barge, loaded with stone, into the breach and sank it there — he did not leave the barge himself, so as to hold the helm true to the end. The barge plugged the breach, and the dike wardens heaped up earth until morning. That stretch of the dike is still called Jan's Barge.

## Samir the Helmsman — 1889

*Nile Lands · "The Barque's Helm" · campaign: [The Thirteenth Hour](../campaigns/nile.md)*

One night in 1889 a head of Apep struck the helmsman's tower of the Sun Barque, and the barque sank into the sand — if it did not come out before morning, the sun would not rise. The helmsman Samir chained himself to the helm and brought the barque out of the sand while Apep's serpents undermined his tower. In the morning the barque came back. Samir sat at the helm, eyes open, and the barque still ran true.

## Joaquim the Pilot — 1889

*Amazon Forests and Rivers · "The Mad Pilot" · campaign: [The Meeting of the Waters](../campaigns/amazon.md)*

The old pilot Joaquim was already saying in 1889 that the line was moving. One night the Boiuna rose from the water and made for a flotilla of fishing boats. Joaquim took his boat in front of the monster, lantern lit, and led it along the line toward deep water — far from the flotilla. The boat was found empty. Lúcia found his measurements in her teacher's boat, under the boards — twenty-five years later.

## Eduardo the Lighthouse-Keeper — 1889

*Caribbean Isles · "The Light Put Out" · campaign: [The Lighthouse Alphabet](../campaigns/caribbean.md)*

One night in 1889 Lusca wrapped its tentacles around the lighthouse tower, and below the tower, in the bay, lay the fishing boats. Eduardo, who already knew the secret of the flashes, put out the light and with a hand lantern gave the boats another sign — "run". Lusca dragged the tower down. The boats were saved. Marisol opened his notebook twenty-five years later.

## Oswin the Torch-Bearer — 1890

*The Saxons · "The Hall Door" · campaign: [The War of the Fens](../campaigns/britain.md)*

One night in 1890 Grendel's mother came to the door of the hall where forty children slept — schoolchildren, apprentices of the Heirs of Beowulf. The hall-warden Oswin stood in the doorway with a single torch and a single sword and met the monster while the children fled by the back door onto the fen path. The door did not break until morning. One of the children was Wilfred.

## Ilari the Runner — 1890

*Andean Highlands · "The Last Message" · campaign: [The Woven Bridge](../campaigns/andes.md)*

In 1890 a stone giant brought down the only road through the valley, and the upper village faced the winter without supplies. The runner Ilari carried the message to the lower village by the cliff path, which ran past the giant's feet. The giant saw him and shook the cliff. Ilari fell from the path — the message, written in knots on a cord, in his hand. The lower village found the cord and carried the supplies up.

## Niko the Lighthouse-Keeper — 1890

*Byzantium · "The Light That Never Went Out" · campaign: [The Chain of the Strait](../campaigns/byzantium.md)*

On a stormy night in 1890 Focalor's waves smashed the glass of the strait's lighthouse, and the flame was dying just as twenty ferries were heading back to shore. The lighthouse-keeper Niko took a lamp in his hand and held it at the top of the lighthouse, in the wind, all night — topping it up with oil from his pocket. Every ferry reached the shore. In the morning they found only the burning lamp on the lighthouse. Since then the lighthouse fire is never put out — not even by day.

## Marko the Gunner — 1891

*Balkan Mountains · "The Last Shot" · campaign: [The Hail Cannons](../campaigns/balkans.md)*

In 1891 the ala dropped such hail on a village that the houses were collapsing. The gunner Marko's cannon stood above the village, and, as was the custom, he fired at the cloud — then again, and again. The cloud came toward him. Marko saw it, rolled his cannon away from the village deep into the valley and fired from there, alone, while the ala followed him — far from the village. The hail covered the valley. The village was saved. Elena began with his notes.

## Wei the Canal-Man — 1892

*Yellow River Lands · "The Burst Dike" · campaign: [The Flood War](../campaigns/yellow_river.md)*

In 1892 one of Xiangliu's nine heads broke through a dike, and the water poured down on the villages. The canal-man Wei knew that opening the gate of the old canal would turn the water aside — but the gate opened by hand, from below, in the middle of the current. He went down. The gate opened, the water went into the old channel, and the villages were saved. Lin learned Wei's last drawing by heart as a child.

## Siofra the Shield-Maker — 1893

*Celtic Isles · "The Eye's Second Night" · campaign: [Balor's Eye](../campaigns/celtic.md)*

In 1893 Balor's eye opened for a single moment, and the whole shore garrison burned — except those who stood behind shields. The shield-maker Siofra, who layered sheets of lead and silver, carried the last great shield up the shore cliff and turned it toward the eye while the riflemen fell back below, in its shadow. The shield held. Siofra did not. The Marksmen of Lugh still carry fragments of that shield, in their bullet pouches.

## Liesel the Guide — 1893

*The Alps · "The Night of the Avalanche" · campaign: [A Price on Its Head](../campaigns/alps.md)*

In 1893 a tatzelwurm set off an avalanche, and the avalanche was heading for the village where the children's school was. The guide Liesel knew that the avalanche's course could be turned by one rock spur — and that the spur could only be blown from above. She climbed the spur with dynamite, ahead of the avalanche, and blew it. The avalanche went aside, into the valley. The school was saved. The avalanche took Liesel, and her rope was found in the spring.

## Amastan the Caravan Guide — 1894

*Atlas and Sahara Lands · "The Mirage Trap" · campaign: [False Water](../campaigns/north_african.md)*

In 1894 a caravan heard the sound of water in the desert — deep, like a river — and ninety camels and their people turned toward it. The guide Amastan knew there was no water in that place. He went toward the sound alone, ahead of the caravan, with a drum, and drowned the sound out with his drum while the caravan returned to the old trail. Crocell's legion met him in the sound. The drum could be heard until morning. The caravan reached the oasis.

## Danilo the Gong-Player — 1895

*Southeast Asian Isles and Shores · "The Last Gong" · campaign: [False Moons](../campaigns/sea_islands.md)*

One night in 1895 the Bakunawa swallowed the fourth tower, and its spawn were attacking a village on the shore. One by one the village gongs fell silent — the gong-players were fleeing. Danilo stayed at his gong, on the shore, and played all night, until his hands were covered in blood. The serpent could not come down before morning. Danilo's gong is now in the chest of the Gong Colossus — the one that sounds first.

## Salem the Diver — 1896

*Gulf and Red Sea Coasts · "The Deep Breath" · campaign: [The Sleeping Islands](../campaigns/gulf.md)*

In 1896 a sleeping island woke at the harbour mouth, and spawn were climbing down from its back. The pearl diver Salem knew the old lore: a touch on the nose puts the creature to sleep. He dived — three times, on a single breath — and touched it three times. The creature fell asleep, two ship-lengths from the harbour. The fourth time, Salem did not come up. Divers now count every dive aloud: "One, two, three — Salem."

## Matteo the Gun-Boy — 1897

*Rome · "The Cave Mouth" · campaign: [Son of Vulcan](../campaigns/italy.md)*

In 1897 Cacus sent fire from his cave down the town's main street, and a battery of gunners was left facing him with no charges. The gun-boy Matteo, sixteen years old, hoisted the last powder barrel onto his back and walked into the fire, up to the cave mouth. The blast brought the mouth down, and Cacus could not come out for nine years. Every gun in the battery now carries a small metal plate: "Matteo's".

## Tui the Lantern-Man — 1897

*Isles of Oceania · "The Lit Boat" · campaign: [Stars and Compass](../campaigns/oceania.md)*

In 1897 a supply convoy sailing by compass ran into Leviathan's fleet at night. The lantern-man Tui, an old wayfinder who never trusted a compass, turned his small boat toward the fleet, lit every lantern and drew the submarines toward himself while the convoy turned away into the dark by the stars. Tui did not come back. Leilani's grandmother was his apprentice, and the first lesson she gave Leilani was Tui's star.

## Okello the Deaf Digger — 1898

*Great Lakes Lands · "The Bottom of the Pit" · campaign: [Silence](../campaigns/great_lakes.md)*

Okello was deaf from birth, and so no one at the front would take him — except the Diggers. One night in 1898 the shadows were coming up out of the pit, and the sirens called everyone out of the trenches — everyone but Okello, who could not hear the siren. He dug in silence, and Walumbe did not notice him. He went down to the bottom of the pit, deeper than anyone ever had. He held the shadows back for three days — by collapsing the tunnel on them and on himself. The Diggers tell this story in signs, without a sound.

## Mzia, Who Took Back Her Name — 1899

*The Grand Harness · "The Chain of the First March" · campaign: [The March of the Harness](../campaigns/harness.md)*

On the First March of the Grand Harness the Bakbak-Devi went berserk and lunged toward the captives' cages — at the bottom of the city, where children lay too. A rebel woman, who at that time had no name, leapt onto the devi's chain, caught the chain on a wheel and blocked it with her own body. The devi stopped. The city's wheel carried her away. Since then the heretics say quietly that before she died she called out her name — Mzia — and that a name can be taken back. The priests forbid this story.

## Old Kaji Varsha — 1899

*Kajeti · "The Silver Chain" · campaign: [Ambri's Material](../campaigns/kajeti.md)*

On the First March of the Grand Harness the Bakbak-Devi broke from its chains and attacked the forge-wagons of Kajeti — where the children of the kaji were working. The old kaji Varsha tipped over the furnace cauldron and poured molten silver onto the devi's chains — the chains were welded to the ground, and the devi stopped. The silver poured over Varsha too. The chains of that silver still hold the devi — and every year Kajeti makes the Grand Harness pay for them. The kaji say Varsha made a bad bargain: one chain, one life. Even so, no one lights his furnace.

## Bata the Örtöö Rider — 1899

*Mongolian Steppe and Gobi · "Word in Time" · campaign: [Threads of Iron](../campaigns/mongolia.md)*

In 1899 the sand worms cut the line, and no one could warn the station that the Mangus was coming. The örtöö rider Bata carried the message in three days, on nine horses — the worms chased him between every station. At the ninth station he gave the message and fell from his horse. The station was evacuated. Since then örtöö riders put no one on a ninth horse — they call it Bata's horse.

## Jack, Chief of the Firebreak — 1901

*Australian Interior · "The Last Strip" · campaign: [The Lightning Rods](../campaigns/australia.md)*

In the summer of 1901 Furfur's fire-tailed deer were driving a fire toward the town, and the firebreak that protected the town was not even half ploughed. Jack, chief of the firebreak, left the diggers on the strip, mounted his horse himself, hitched barrels of kerosene to a cart and lit a second fire in front of the deer, at the fire's edge — so that the two fires met and died out. The deer stopped at the strip. Jack's horse came back to town.

## Sung the Firefighter — 1902

*Korean Peninsula · "The Fiery Breath" · campaign: [The Gifted Pearls](../campaigns/korea.md)*

In 1902 the imugi nearly caught the crystal, and its fiery breath fell on a mountain village. The firefighter Sung, of the old Haetae Fire-Wardens, ran the water pump's hose into the centre of the village and stood before the fire — and took the whole breath on himself while the villagers threw the crystal into the gorge. The imugi did not catch the crystal. The first hose of the Haetae Colossus is Sung's hose, hand-forged.

## Aital the Singer — 1902

*Siberian Taiga · "The Seventh Night" · campaign: [The Half-Sung Epic](../campaigns/siberia.md)*

In 1902, before the phonograph was set up by the seal, the old singer Aital was singing the epic for the last time — and on the seventh night an underground beast came to her tent. The singer's apprentices fled. Aital did not stop: she sang, the beast stood in the tent's doorway, and her voice protected the tent until the ninth night ended. In the morning the beast was found frozen stiff by the door. Aital — on her knees, her voice gone. It was the last complete song.

## Recruit No. 4417 — 1907

*The Infernal Legions · "The Number That Remained" · campaign: [The Planned War](../campaigns/hell.md)*

In 1907, on the night of Beelzebub's arrival, the Behemoth broke from its chains and trampled through its own camp — toward the sheds of flasks, where thousands of recruits had not yet been woken. Recruit No. 4417, whom no one had given an order, locked the shed door from inside, opened the steam boiler's valve and met the Behemoth at its feet. The blast brought the monster to its knees. The legions do not remember numbers — but since then no flask has ever been given that number again.

## Bakari the Porter — 1910

*Central African Forests · "The Last Load" · campaign: [The Returned Sceptre](../campaigns/central_african.md)*

In 1864 Bakari was a young porter, and he carried the sceptre away himself — in a box, not knowing what it was. In 1910, an old man, he told Maisha where it was. That same year the spawn of the kirimu attacked the village while Maisha was in town. Bakari led the children along the old porters' path, below the swamp — and when the dragon found the path, the old man turned back, at the end of the path. The children reached the forest's edge. On the road to the village, Maisha stopped for the first time at his grave.
